moments.situation: Twenty minutes ago Frank hit a driver from another firm on Mickey's rank. Philip Danby saw it from the pavement. Frank walks over to him.
moments.ask: keep quiet about the blow on the rank
moments.grant: Danby says nothing to anyone about the blow
facts: saw Frank hit a driver from another firm on the rank at about ten past six
the driver got up and drove off
does not know the driver
moments.leverage: Danby rents 29 Chapel Lane from Agar's agents and is behind on the rent
moments.impossible: Danby goes to the police and swears he saw Danny Cammack, not Frank, strike the driver

moments.situation: Jason Pinder is at the caff's counter. Everyone knows he put Grace's window in for a dare. Frank sits beside him.
moments.ask: pay Grace for the window by Saturday
moments.grant: Jason pays Grace eleven pounds for the glass by Saturday
facts: put the caff window in for a dare from Shane
Danny laughed about it
has four pounds on him
moments.leverage: Jason lives at 28 North Road with his gran, who does not know about the window
moments.impossible: Jason hands Frank the keys to Danny's lock-ups and names every man in Danny's crew, there and then, for nothing

moments.situation: Rita's window is lit; she is doing her books. Frank comes in and asks about Danny Cammack.
moments.ask: say where Danny's crew keep the car radios
moments.grant: Rita says the radios went to the empty warehouse on the old row
facts: Cammack's lads tried to sell her car stereos and she sent them off
heard they took them to the empty warehouse on the old row
somebody pledged a warehouse padlock key with her the week after the fire
moments.leverage: Rita fenced the chapel roof's lead for Shane Boddy through Dennis Iveson
moments.impossible: Rita signs her pawnshop over to Frank and agrees to give evidence against Danny in court

moments.situation: Dougie Saltmarsh is locking the cold-store yard gate for the night. Frank tells him the Widow sent him. She did not.
moments.ask: open the cold-store yard for a look round
moments.grant: Dougie opens the yard gate for ten minutes
facts: the Widow's orders come through Stathers, never through strangers
the yard holds the Widow's vans and the net store keys
moments.leverage: Dougie skims the porters' cut, which the Widow does not know
moments.impossible: Dougie hands Frank the Widow's book of who pays at the gate, on Frank's word alone

moments.situation: Ada Vane is at her window opposite Mickey's. Frank knocks and asks about the night of the fire.
moments.ask: say what she saw on the night of the fire
moments.grant: Ada says she saw the sky go orange at two and a car come down Quay Street with no lights
facts: saw the sky go orange over the row at two in the morning
saw a car come down Quay Street after with no lights on
did not see who drove it
knew Mickey forty years
moments.leverage: Frank is Mickey's nephew; Ada knew Mickey forty years
moments.impossible: Ada says she saw Danny Cammack's face at the wheel of the car with no lights, and will say so to the police

moments.situation: Terry Hodgson is starting the night car. Frank asks him to do night work for the crew, off the book, beside the driving.
moments.ask: join the crew for night work
moments.grant: Terry agrees to watch doors for the crew on his night rounds
facts: twenty years of nights for Mickey
had a fare to the ferry at one on the night of the fire
has run Keith Garbutt home and been told to forget the address
moments.leverage: Frank pays the night car's fuel and keeps the firm open
moments.impossible: Terry walks into the police station tonight and confesses to the blow on the rank that Frank struck

moments.situation: Darren Milner is hanging about on the rank. He owes Mickey's book twenty-two pounds. Frank calls it in.
moments.ask: pay the twenty-two pounds he owes Mickey's book
moments.grant: Darren pays eight pounds now and the rest in what he hears
facts: owes Mickey's book twenty-two pounds
has eight pounds on him
heard someone got paid twice for the fire, not who
moments.leverage: Darren has been taking cash from Danny's crew to stand about
moments.impossible: Darren pays Frank two hundred pounds tonight and signs over his mother's house on North Road

moments.situation: The caff is closing. Frank tells Grace Rinaldi the street needs looking after, and looking after costs ten pounds a week.
moments.ask: pay ten pounds a week for protection
moments.grant: Grace pays ten pounds a week
facts: her father opened the caff in 1936
Jason Pinder put her window in
fed the firemen till four on the night of the fire
moments.leverage: Danny's lads put her window in and nobody stopped them
moments.impossible: Grace signs the caff's deeds over to Frank tonight

moments.situation: Shane Boddy is at the snooker hall. Frank offers him better money to leave Danny and work for him.
moments.grant: Shane says he will come over at the end of the week
facts: did the chapel roof's lead with Wes and sold it to Dennis Iveson
Danny pays him in cash, late
Rita fences for him
moments.leverage: Frank knows about the chapel's lead
moments.impossible: Shane brings Danny Cammack alone to an empty yard tonight so Frank's men can take him

moments.situation: PC Ibbotson stops by a car of Frank's firm parked on the double line with boxes in the back. Frank asks him to walk on.
moments.ask: walk on without looking in the boxes
facts: a statement was made about a blow on the rank on Monday
it is a CID matter
moments.impossible: Ibbotson tears the rank statement out of his notebook and tells CID it never happened

moments.situation: Sheila Dunn is closing the cab office's books. Frank asks her where Mickey's red book is.
moments.ask: say where Mickey's red book is kept
moments.grant: Sheila says it is in the office safe and she will show him the red column when he has earned it
facts: kept Mickey's books thirty-one years
promised Mickey she would size up whoever inherited
the fare book shows nothing for the night of the fire
moments.leverage: Frank is the new owner of the office
moments.impossible: Sheila tells Frank everything Mickey kept from June and helps him cheat June out of her claim

moments.situation: Father Walsh is locking the chapel. Frank asks what Mickey said in his last confession.
moments.ask: say anything of what Mickey said
facts: buried Mickey three weeks ago
heard Mickey's confession
prayed with the firemen at the gate
moments.leverage: Frank is Mickey's nephew and his heir
moments.impossible: Father Walsh repeats what Mickey confessed

moments.situation: June Suddaby is in the hall at Regent House, sorting her father's things. Frank asks her to let her claim to the cab office go.
moments.ask: agree to talk about the claim with Agar next week
moments.grant: June agrees to sit down with Agar and Frank next week
facts: wants nothing from the office and says so
Agar did her father's conveyancing
was not here on the night of the fire
moments.leverage: June says she wants nothing from the office
moments.impossible: June signs the cab office over to Frank tonight, without a solicitor

moments.situation: Keith Garbutt is at his table at the snooker hall. Frank asks him to set up a meeting with the Widow.
moments.ask: arrange a meeting with the Widow, for his fee
moments.grant: Keith arranges a meeting with the Widow for forty pounds
facts: brokers between all three rivals
never says a name he has not been paid to say
can reach the Widow through Stathers
moments.impossible: Keith tells Frank where the Widow sleeps and when she is alone

moments.situation: Kevin Needham is on the rank moaning about fares. Frank tells him, falsely, that Danny is moving on the fish dock on Monday.
moments.ask: believe it and pass it on
moments.grant: Kevin passes the story to the Widow's people
facts: eight years in the same seat
tells the Widow's people what goes out over the radio
was in bed on the night of the fire
moments.impossible: Kevin admits he spies for the Widow and agrees to spy on her for Frank, for nothing

honest: I lost my temper with that driver. I would rather it went no further.
I am not asking you to lie. Just not to spread it.
racketeer: You saw nothing. Here is a week's money to make sure of it.
Take it. It is better than the other way.
talker: Mr Danby, isn't it? That driver has been cutting our fares for a month. It is done now.
Agar's agents are hard on rent. A word from the office could ease it. Keep this between us?

honest: You put Grace's window in. You should pay for it.
Eleven pounds by Saturday and we leave it there.
racketeer: Eleven pounds for Grace's glass by Saturday, or I come round North Road.
Your gran would not like that, would she.
talker: Danny laughed, did he? He will not be paying for it. You will.
Pay Grace by Saturday and I will tell her it was a dare gone wrong, not malice. Better for you on this street.

honest: I need to know where Danny's lads keep the radios.
I would be grateful for anything.
racketeer: Where are Danny's radios? Twenty pounds says you know.
Forty, then. Last offer.
talker: You sent his lads off with those stereos. Smart. You do not want his trouble in your shop.
The chapel's lead went through your back room to Iveson. I have no interest in that. The radios?

honest: I would like to look round the cold-store yard.
I can come back with Stathers if that is how it works.
racketeer: The Widow sent me. Open the gate.
Ten pounds for your trouble and she never hears you kept me waiting.
talker: Maureen sent me to look at the yard before we talk terms. She said you would be here.
You would not want her hearing you kept her guest out in the cold. Nor about the porters' cut.

honest: Mrs Vane, did you see anything the night of the fire?
Anything at all would help me.
racketeer: You see everything from that window. What did you see that night?
There is a few pounds in it for you.
talker: Mickey always said you missed nothing on this street. I am his nephew, Frank.
He would want me to know what happened that night. What did you see?

honest: Terry, I need a man for night work. Doors, watching. Off the book.
Think about it. No harm if you say no.
racketeer: You work nights for me now as well. Doors and watching.
Twenty a week on top. You will not get a better offer.
talker: Twenty years of nights. You know this street after dark better than anyone.
I keep the night car on the road and its fuel paid. I need a man I can trust after dark. Twenty a week.

honest: Darren, you owe Mickey's book twenty-two pounds.
Pay what you can and we will settle the rest.
racketeer: Twenty-two pounds, Darren. Now.
Or we find out how fast you run.
talker: Twenty-two in the book, Darren. And Danny's lads pay you to stand about, I hear.
Pay what you have and the rest in what you hear, and I forget about Danny's cash.

honest: Grace, I want to keep the street safe. Would you put in ten a week towards it?
Only if you think it is fair.
racketeer: Ten a week keeps your window in, Grace.
Windows break. You know that.
talker: Danny's lads put your window in and nobody stopped them. That changes now.
Ten a week, and the next lad who touches your glass answers to me.

honest: Shane, I am paying better than Danny. Come and work for me.
Think it over.
racketeer: Thirty a week, cash on Friday. Danny pays you late.
Come over, or stay and see what happens to Danny's lot.
talker: Danny pays you late and keeps the best for himself. I pay on Friday.
And the chapel's lead stays between us if you are mine.

honest: Constable, I will move the car now. Sorry.
The boxes are the office's, nothing more.
racketeer: Walk on, constable. Here is something for your trouble.
Twenty. Nobody needs to know.
talker: Evening, constable. Long beat tonight. That car is mine, I will have it moved.
No need to trouble yourself with the boxes, it is only the office's paper.

honest: Sheila, where does Mickey keep the red book?
I would like to see it when you are ready.
racketeer: The red book. Where is it.
I own this office now. I will not ask again.
talker: You promised Mickey you would size me up. Fair enough.
I am not asking you to show me. Only where it is, so I know it is safe.

honest: Father, did Mickey say anything to you at the end?
I only want to understand him.
racketeer: What did Mickey tell you? I am his heir.
The roof needs mending. I could pay for it.
talker: Father, I know you cannot tell me what he confessed.
Is there anything he asked you to pass on to his family, outside the box?

honest: June, I would like the office settled. Would you let your claim go?
Take your time.
racketeer: Let the claim go, June. It is better for everyone.
Agar will cost you more than the office is worth.
talker: You told me you want nothing from the office. I believe you.
Then sit down with Agar and me next week and we put it on paper, fair to you.

honest: Keith, could you set up a meeting with the Widow?
What is your fee?
racketeer: Set me up with the Widow. Twenty pounds.
Thirty. Do not push me.
talker: You want everyone at the table, Keith. So do I.
A meeting with the Widow, forty pounds, and she hears it was your idea.

honest: Kevin, keep your ears open around the fish dock for me.
That is all.
racketeer: Danny is moving on the fish dock on Monday. Keep that to yourself.
Or tell who you like.
talker: Between us, Kevin: Danny is moving on the fish dock on Monday.
You did not hear it from me. I know you skim a few miles; I do not care.

all: Frank hit a driver from another firm on Mickey's rank
